data.source_title: A Novel Approach to Addressing an Unintended Consequence of Direct to Room: The Delay of Initial Vital Signs
data.locator: Abstract and Methods/Results; TTVS defined as quick registration to first documented vital sign.
data.source_setting: Single academic tertiary ED, Staten Island University Hospital, New York; ambulatory entry via quick registration and direct-to-room or formal triage pathways.
data.source_period: Control 2014-11-01 to 2015-05-01; intervention 2015-11-01 to 2016-05-01; included 07:00-23:00 arrivals.
data.quantity: Mean time from quick registration to first documented vital sign
data.source_evidence_basis: Retrospective before-after cohort reports means and Ns; intervention placed a patient-care assistant at a waiting-area vital-sign station coupled to quick registration.
data.limitations: Single-center nonrandomized before/after implementation and restricted hours; pre/post cohort dates are a year apart. Does not quantify identity verification failure, completion of full triage, or effects in EMS arrivals. Source reports35% reduction; rounded endpoint means15.3 and9.8 imply about35.95%. Preserve reported value rather than treat it as a recomputed rate.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model quick demographic/chief-complaint registration, initial vital signs, and formal nurse triage as distinct events; use the pre/post timing only as an external workflow scenario, never as RWJ timing.
